n: Christmas duck with red cabbage and potato dumplings (duck breast)
z: For four servings use 800 g boneless raw duck breast with skin, not a whole duck. For the red cabbage, slice the cabbage finely. Dice 100 g onion and the apple, sweat in 20 g butter, add the cabbage, vinegar, sugar, cloves, 1 bay leaf and about 200 ml water. Cover and braise for 60–75 minutes until soft, adding water if needed; remove the cloves and bay leaf before serving. Meanwhile boil the peeled floury potatoes for 20–25 minutes, drain, let the steam escape and press through a ricer. While lukewarm, mix with egg, potato starch and salt; shape 8 dumplings and let them cook in gently simmering salted water for 15–20 minutes without boiling. Score the duck skin in a diamond pattern without cutting into the meat. Salt, place skin-side down in a cold pan and render the fat over medium heat for 8–12 minutes. Turn, sear for 2 minutes, then finish in a preheated oven at 160 °C (conventional) for about 20–30 minutes until the core reaches at least 70 °C for 2 minutes. Rest for 5 minutes. For the sauce, pour off excess fat and brown the remaining onion, carrot and tomato paste in the pan juices. Deglaze with 300 ml water and the stock powder, add the second bay leaf, reduce for about 15 minutes, remove the bay leaf and strain. Slice the duck and serve with red cabbage, 2 dumplings each and the sauce.

n: Autumn venison stew with red wine, mushrooms and lingonberries
z: Pat the venison dry and cut into cubes of about 3 cm. Dice the onions and carrots and quarter the mushrooms. Sear the meat in batches in hot sunflower oil and set aside. Brown the onions and carrots in the pot and briefly fry the tomato paste. Deglaze with 300 ml dry red wine and reduce for about 5 minutes. Add 400 ml water and the stock powder and return the meat to the pot. Lightly crush the juniper berries and put them with the bay leaves into a spice bag. Cover and braise over low heat for about 90–120 minutes until tender, adding water if needed. Add the mushrooms for the last 20 minutes. Remove the spice bag, stir in the cream and lingonberries and reduce the sauce uncovered for about 10 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Made with red wine; braising does not reliably make the dish alcohol-free. Contains sulphites. Amounts are for the stew without a side dish; braising time depends on the cut.

Dice the beef, bring to a boil with 1.5 l water and salt, skim and simmer gently for about 90 minutes. Grate the beetroot and carrots, dice the onion and sweat in oil; add the tomato paste and vinegar. Add diced potatoes and finely shredded white cabbage to the broth, add the sautéed vegetables after 10 minutes and cook for another 20–30 minutes until the meat and vegetables are tender. Add garlic and dill, season with salt and pepper and serve with sour cream. No beans; the total time includes simmering the beef.

n: Fried pirozhki with potatoes and mushrooms
z: For about 12 pirozhki (3 per serving): knead flour, dry yeast, sugar, salt, 250 ml lukewarm water and 20 g oil into a soft dough. Cover and let rise for about 60 minutes; meanwhile make the filling and let it cool. Peel the potatoes, boil until soft and mash. Fry finely chopped mushrooms and onion in a little oil until the liquid has evaporated, mix into the potatoes and season. Divide the dough into 12 pieces, flatten, fill and seal the edges firmly. Rest for 10 minutes, then fry in batches in hot sunflower oil over medium heat until golden on both sides and the dough is cooked through. The 80 g oil include 20 g in the dough and about 60 g for the filling and frying; keep extra oil ready depending on your pan.

n: Fried pirozhki with cabbage and carrots
z: For about 12 pirozhki (3 per serving): knead flour, dry yeast, sugar, salt, 250 ml lukewarm water and 20 g oil into a soft dough. Cover and let rise for about 60 minutes; meanwhile make the filling and let it cool. Finely shred the white cabbage, grate the carrots and dice the onion. Braise in a little oil for about 20 minutes until soft; let excess liquid evaporate and season. Divide the dough into 12 pieces, flatten, fill and seal the edges firmly. Rest for 10 minutes, then fry in batches in hot sunflower oil over medium heat until golden on both sides and the dough is cooked through. The 80 g oil include 20 g in the dough and about 60 g for the filling and frying; keep extra oil ready depending on your pan.

n: Kotlety with mashed potatoes and cream sauce
z: Soak the bread roll in 100 ml milk. Mix with ground beef, egg, half of the finely chopped onion, salt and pepper and shape 8 kotlety. Fry in oil on both sides until cooked through. Meanwhile peel the potatoes, boil for about 20 minutes until soft, drain and mash with 150 ml warm milk and 30 g butter. For the sauce, sweat the remaining onion in the pan juices with 10 g butter, stir in the flour, deglaze with 200 ml water and the stock powder, add the cream and simmer for a few minutes. Serve 2 kotlety per person with mash and sauce.

n: Qabeli palau – Afghan pulao with lamb
z: Rinse the basmati rice and soak in water for 30 minutes. Dice the lamb, brown in half of the oil, add the onion and season with salt, pepper and half of the cumin and cardamom. Cover with about 700 ml water and braise gently for 75–90 minutes until tender. Meanwhile cut the carrots into thin strips, fry in the remaining oil, briefly fry the raisins and sugar with them and set aside. Drain the rice, par-boil in fresh salted water for about 5–7 minutes and drain. Layer the meat and rice in a heavy pot, add about 200 ml strained cooking liquid and the remaining spices; spread the carrots and raisins on top. Cover tightly and steam over the lowest heat for 20–25 minutes, then rest for 10 minutes.

n: High-protein spinach and feta breakfast rolls
z: Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Sweat the onion in oil, fry the ground chicken for 8 minutes, season and let cool. Whisk the eggs and stir in the meat, spinach, feta and part of the mozzarella. Mix in the almond flour, coconut flour and baking powder, place 12 rolls on a baking tray, sprinkle with mozzarella and bake for 13–15 minutes until golden.

Mix the ground chicken with paprika, pepper and salt. Halve the nori sheets, spread the filling thinly, brush the edges with egg and roll up. Cut into pieces, brush with egg, sprinkle with sesame and bake at 200 °C for about 15 minutes (core temperature at least 74 °C).

Cut the broccoli into florets, blanch for 5 minutes and drain. Preheat the oven to 180 °C, press the florets flat on baking paper, season, sprinkle with cheese and bake for about 10 minutes until the cheese is golden.
